hints: There are n! arrangements if all letters had unique labels.
Swapping equal letters does not create a new visible string.
Divide by count(letter)! for every letter's frequency.
analogy: Pretend repeated letters have labels, count arrangements, then remove the label-only reorderings.
example: For aab, 3!/2!=3 distinct strings: aab, aba, baa.
algorithm: Compute n! times the modular inverse factorial of every character frequency modulo 1,000,000,007.
correctness: Each visible string is counted exactly as many times as the product of factorials of repeated-letter counts among labeled permutations.
complexity: O(n+alphabet) time and O(n) factorial storage, or O(alphabet) with modular exponentiation.
